cells.tense: You are here with the pen, letting a long commitment show you what it's made of.
cells.ask: Take a few minutes with something you've kept with and enjoy what it has turned into. No fixing, no improving — let having looked after it stand as enough.
cells.core:
You stay with things by adjusting them as you go. That isn't drift — it's you keeping a commitment alive by sensing what it needs this month and what it can do without. Nothing is being forced. What you've looked after has accumulated into something you can stand next to without holding it up, and today that's simply true.

There's a thing you've stayed with that you'd deeply miss if it went. Before the week crowds in, give it a few minutes of straight enjoyment. Let what it has become and what you did to get it there sit together. Other things will keep asking for attention and you'll get to them — but the grown part is allowed to be what you look at first.

cells.tense: You are bracing toward a future that can't be written in, and the grip has gone rigid.
cells.act: give directions plainly, once, and let them walk
cells.ask: Tell someone how you got through a hard thing you've already come through — plain, one time, no follow-up needed — then let them walk it on their own.
cells.core:
You stay with things by gripping harder, and the grip has turned into testing. Every commitment has to keep proving it's still real, so nothing gets the dignity of being finished. The pull is toward the next version of it, the better form, the one that would finally be settled — and the version you have keeps getting audited instead of lived in. From where you stand that reads as devotion.

You know a passage through something difficult, and someone near you is lost on that exact route. Tell them how you got through — plainly, one time — and then let their feet do the walking. Handing over a direction without carrying the person is the move your grip has forgotten how to make.

cells.tense: You are still at a door that has already closed behind you, not walking through.
cells.act: share your strength where it is needed
cells.ask: Carry something concrete for someone this week — a ride, a meal, a form filled out — hand it over whole, and when it's finished let it stay finished.
cells.core:
The staying-power has thinned, and what's left is mostly standing still. The commitments are still named — the routines, the roles, the things you said yes to — but your weight isn't in them anymore. You keep the outer form of a dedication, and the live part is somewhere else. From inside it feels like there's nothing left to give. From anywhere else, it looks like a person who hasn't crossed.

There's a way back that doesn't ask you to push harder. Carry one bounded thing for someone who needs it — a ride, a meal you can make, a form you can fill out — hand it over complete, and stop. Helping something with an end reminds you what choosing feels like. Your dedication runs on choice, not on showing up out of habit.

cells.tense: You are at the pen without noticing, writing commitments you file under habit.
cells.act: rest in the result of the tending
cells.ask: Look at one commitment that quietly turned out well and let yourself rest in it. The adjustments that kept it alive were choices you made, on time, one after another.
cells.core:
You hold things together through friction — deciding when to press, when to yield, when to say the sentence that unsticks it — and you write it off as circumstance. The adjustments that keep a commitment alive get filed under going along with things, or being built that way, or nobody else stepping up. The choices are still there in what you've carried. The times you stayed, when you could have gone, don't get counted because you didn't experience them as decisions.

Go back to the pleasure of the thing. Sit with one commitment that quietly turned out well and look at it as yours. Not a plan, not a project — just resting in the fact that you made it what it is. Hold that a while and your own hand becomes visible in what you've been carrying.

A reader could reasonably say the quitting behind Too Little was chosen after something specific, so that cell stays on the present shape of the standing-still and says nothing about what happened there. The asks survive a wrong read: each is an act the person can do anyway and learn from, not a repair conditional on my being right. The sentence that serves me more than them is the Too Much 'nobody gets either offer cleanly' — clever, but it collects a debt for the writer; I cut it.

attempts.check: The record says the person holds their commitments through active rebalancing, not that any particular commitment has failed or been underappreciated by others, so no cell may assert an outcome in someone else's eyes. A reader could reasonably say the Too Little withdrawal was chosen after something specific happened and the person knows exactly what — so that cell must stay on the present shape of standing still and say nothing about a cause, a cost, or a history. All four asks are acts the person can do whether or not my read is right, and each one teaches them something about this capacity even if the read is off. The sentence that serves me more than them is the Too Much line about 'nothing gets to rest' — it's a neat closing image that collects a debt for the writer, so it's cut. The Unacknowledged cell's 'not luck' was certifying the person from outside their own account; the rewrite offers the credit as a thing they can hold rather than a verdict I pass. The status 4 ask was also doing the house's pet move — speak it to someone — when the medicine's own act is taking pleasure, which needs no audience.
